4.text: The Chukchee do not approve of diluting alcohol with much water. I have

5.text: witnessed them drink large glasses of 95% alcohol, one drop of which was

6.text: sufficient to make my mouth burn for several minutes. Even the unrefined

7.text: alcohol of the Kolyma country is drunk undiluted when possible. The so-called

8.text: “principal chief” of the Reindeer Chukchee, previously mentioned,¹ died sud-

9.text: denly in 1898 on the day of his arrival at the town of Sredne-Kolymsk, after

10.text: a generous drink of unrectified alcohol.

11.text: The Reindeer people are more eager for liquor than the Maritime. This

12.text: may be because they have less chance to satisfy their craving. When they

13.text: know that there is some strong liquor within their reach, most of them are

14.text: ready to pay an exorbitant price for it. I was assured by many that if necessary

15.text: they would be quite ready to give a piece of their own flesh for a drink.

16.text: Small wooden kegs, in which the liquor is brought from the Russian

17.text: settlements, are carefully washed with hot water, and if possible boiled in large

18.text: kettles. I have seen people sitting

19.text: around a keg, which finally refused

20.text: to yield any more, weep bitter tears

21.text: over the end of their festivity.
